DECISION 
I. 
INTRODUCTION 
A. 
SUMMARY 
The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (Authority or PURA) allocates $3,006,596 
in grants from the Public, Educational and Governmental Programming and Education 
Technology Investment Account (PEGPETIA). The Authority awards PEGPETIA funds 
accumulated through February 22, 2024, in this proceeding, with $1,503,301 for 39 grants 
to support public, educational, and governmental programming (PEG Grants) and 
$1,503,295 for 74 grants to support educational technology initiatives (ETI Grants). 
B. 
BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING 
In 2007, the General Assembly established the PEGPETIA program to promote 
and improve public, educational, and governmental programming and to support 
education technology initiatives. See Public Act No. 07-253, § 33, codified as General 
Statutes § 16-331cc. The program is funded by a quarterly tax on the gross earnings of 
video service providers. General Statutes § 16-331cc. 
The Authority conducts an annual proceeding to determine the allocation of the 
accumulated funding in the account and to administer grants to eligible entities. The 
Authority established the application requirements through a contested proceeding in 
2008 and revised the requirements in 2019. Decision, Mar. 26, 2008, Docket No. 07-10-
11, DPUC Proceeding to Establish Administrative Guidelines for the Public Educational 
and Governmental Programming and Educational Technology Investment Account 
Pursuant to Public Act 07-253 (Guidelines Decision); Decision, Oct. 23, 2019, Docket No. 
07-10-11RE01, DPUC Proceeding to Establish Administrative Guidelines for the Public 
Educational and Governmental Programming and Education Technology Investment 
Account – Grant Eligibility Criteria and Guidelines (Revised Guidelines Decision); General 
Statutes § 16-331cc(d). 
C. 
CONDUCT OF THE PROCEEDING 
On September 12, 2023, the Authority issued a Notice of Proceeding, directing its 
Office of Education, Outreach, and Enforcement (EOE) to file a notice regarding the 
application process, conduct the initial review or applications, and file a motion requesting 
the issuance of a proposed decision. 
The Authority received a total of 117 applications, filed as motions, during the 
application window, October 2, 2023, through February 29, 2024.1 On March 25, 2024, 
EOE filed a motion with a draft proposed decision. 

1 The Authority extended the initial application deadline of February 22, 2024, to February 29, 2024. Motion 
Ruling No. 119, Mar. 25, 2024. 

Docket No. 23-10-02 

Page 2 

The Authority issued a proposed final decision in this matter on April 11, 2024. All 
participants were given the opportunity to file written exceptions to the proposed final 
decision. 
D. 
PARTICIPANTS 
A list of participants is attached as Appendix A. 
II. 
AUTHORITY ANALYSIS 
A. 
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA 
The Authority awards 50% of PEGPETIA grant funding to: (1) local community 
antenna television and video advisory councils; (2) the state-wide video advisory council; 
(3) public, educational, and governmental programmers; and (4) public, educational, and 
governmental studio operators, “to subsidize capital and equipment costs related to 
producing and procuring [public, educational and governmental] programming.” General 
Statutes § 16-331cc(b). The Authority awards the remaining 50% “to boards of education 
and other education entities for education technology initiatives.” Id. 
The PEG grant funding is intended to promote and improve public, educational, 
and governmental access programming in Connecticut. Guidelines Decision, p. 2. 
Although funds are available to a wide variety of entities involved either directly or 
indirectly in producing community access programs, the awarding of funds to those 
entities is not the goal of the program. Id. PEG grant funds should be used for capital 
and equipment costs that aid the production or procurement of public, educational, and 
governmental programs. Accordingly, after receiving a PEG grant, recipients must file a 
report with the Authority, stating: (a) the title, subject, and duration (in minutes) of all 
community access programs facilitated in whole or in part by the grant award; (b) how the 
programs were distributed through community access channels; and (c) the protocols for 
ensuring that any programs produced with equipment purchased with PEGPETIA funds 
are made available to the applicant’s local PEG studio. To ensure the funding is used 
appropriately, after completion of the project, PEG grant recipients must also file a report 
of the project enabled by the grant funds. 
The ETI grant funding is intended to support education technology initiatives of 
boards of education and other education entities. Both public and private schools are 
eligible to apply for PEGPETIA funds. Guidelines Decision, p. 14. To ensure the funding 
is used appropriately, after completion of the project, ETI grant recipients must file a report 
of the project enabled by the grant funds. 
B. 
APPLICATIONS AND ELIGIBILITY REVIEW 
In this docket, 117 applications were submitted, including 41 applications for PEG 
Grants and 76 applications for ETI Grants. The Authority awards a total of $1,503,301 in 
39 PEG Grants and a total of $1,503,295 in 74 ETI Grants. The PEG grants support the 
promotion and improvement of public, educational, and governmental programming, and 
the ETI grants support education technology initiatives. General Statutes § 16-331cc. 

Docket No. 23-10-02 

Page 3 

The Children’s Space is ineligible for failure to provide a complete application, 
including supporting documentation for the cost of the investment or initiative. Applicants 
must submit complete applications and meet the eligibility requirements established in 
the Guidelines Decision and Revised Guidelines Decision. On March 4, 2024, EOE 
issued correspondence, reminding all applicants that, as stated in the PEGPETIA Grant 
Application, supporting documentation is required for each item listed in the proposed 
budget sheet.2 In that correspondence, EOE noted that applications without supporting 
documentation, i.e., a copy of the bid, estimate, or quote, would be considered 
incomplete. Even if it were complete, the application from The Children’s Space would 
not qualify for an ETI grant award. As noted in the Authority’s PEGPETIA Educational 
Grant Guidance, issued November 20, 2019, the General Assembly’s education 
technology goals provide guidance for determining ETI grant eligibility. The Children’s 
Space is a childcare center that, at the time of its application, had enrolled 6 children, 
ages 3-5. In its application, the Children’s Center sought funding for 2 iPad pro tablets 
and accessories, to be used by teachers to track student activities, complete lesson plans, 
and allow children to play education games. Such use is not an educational technology 
initiative that advances a goal or core focus area related to education technology. 
Two applicants are ineligible due to non-compliance with one or more of the 
Authority’s orders relating to prior grant awards. The Authority awarded PEG Grants and 
ETI Grants in Docket Nos. 19-11-01, 21-10-13, and 22-10-02. Grants awarded in each 
of those dockets were accompanied by orders requiring compliance filings, including 
documentation of expenses and reports regarding the proper use of awarded funds. To 
ensure the integrity of the PEGPETIA program, applicants must demonstrate compliance 
with any orders accompanying prior grants. Non-compliance with previous orders may 
disqualify an applicant from receiving funds through the current cycle.3 There is no 
indication that Griswold Public Schools complied with Order Nos. 2 and 4 in Docket No. 
21-10-13. There is also no indication that Shiloh Baptist Church complied with Order Nos. 
2, 3, and 4 in Docket No. 21-10-13.4 Accordingly, Griswold Public School and Shiloh 
Baptist Church are ineligible to receive a grant in this docket because they have not 
demonstrated compliance with orders relating to their receipt of prior PEGPETIA grant 
awards. 
Faith CD Corporation is also ineligible for a PEG Grant. First, it is not at all clear 
from the application that the grant funds would be used to support the promotion or 
improvement of public, educational, and governmental programming. Second, as 
indicated by Rocky Hill Community TV (RHCTV), Shiloh Baptist Church and Faith CD 
Corporation share the same address and share at least some personnel. RHCTV 
Exceptions, p. 2. RHCTV notes that the “Authorized individual on the Shiloh Church

application is also a Principal for the Faith CD Corporation.” Id. In addition, the “Director 
on the Shiloh application is also a principal of the Faith CD Corporation.” Id. Shiloh 
Baptist Church received a grant award in Docket No. 21-10-13, but never complied with 
orders requiring (1) copies of receipts for expended grant funds, (2) a report of the 
community access programs facilitated by the grant funds, or (3) an overall account of 
the project enabled by the grant funds. Accordingly, Faith CD Corporation and Shiloh 
Baptist Church will continue to be ineligible in future PEGPETIA grant cycles until all 
outstanding compliance has been filed in Docket No. 21-10-13.

C. 
ALLOCATION OF PEGPETIA FUNDS 
For the grant cycle in this docket, $3,006,662 is available in the PEGPETIA 
account. The Authority awards half of the funding in PEG Grants for capital and 
equipment costs related to producing and procuring public, educational and governmental 
programming, and the Authority awards half of the funding in ETI Grants for education 
technology initiatives. General Statutes § 16-331cc(b). PEG Grants are available to (1) 
local community antenna television and video advisory councils, (2) the state-wide video 
advisory council (3) public, educational, and governmental programmers, and (4) public, 
educational, and governmental studio operators. Id. ETI Grants are available to boards 
of education and other education entities. Id. 
The Authority received 117 applications for PEGPETIA grants, with 4 applicants 
deemed wholly ineligible. The 39 eligible PEG Grant applicants sought a total of 
$4,348,165.63 for public, educational, and governmental programming. The 74 eligible 
ETI Grant applicants sought $11,161,306.75 for education technology initiatives. Over 
20% of the budget items in those applications were for costs that are ineligible for 
PEGPETIA funding, such as expenses for permitting, travel, lodging, and salaries. See 
Guidelines Decision, pp. 3-4. PEGPETIA grant funds may not be used on non-equipment 
costs such as salaries, service agreements, or stipends. As noted in the application, non-
equipment costs, such as design and engineering, installation, training, warranties, or 
insurance, must be reasonable and should be limited to less than 10% of the overall grant. 
Software may be categorized as equipment.

The awarded PEGPETIA grant funds may be applied toward any capital expense 
listed in the application, with less than 10% used for non-equipment costs.5 As a result 
of the cap on both types of grants, some recipients may need to scale down their original 
project plans and complete a smaller version of the proposed project. The PEGPETIA 
grant funds must be returned to the DEEP Business Office if a recipient is unable to either 
(1) scale down their project or (2) complete the project with other available funding. If 
alterations other than to scale must be made to implement a smaller version of a 
recipient’s project, the recipient should file a motion requesting approval of the change. 
Any unused funds must be returned to the DEEP Business Office prior to receiving 
a new grant award. 

5 EOE applied a 10% maximum on installation cost requests for applicants requesting more than $65,000, 
which is reflected in EOE’s disallowed cost calculation. See Motion No. 120, Attachment 1.

III. 
CONCLUSION AND ORDERS 
A. 
CONCLUSION 
The Authority awards PEG Grants and ETI Grants to the 113 recipients identified in 
Tables 2 and 3, above, in the amounts identified in the respective tables. PEG grant funds 
should be used for capital and equipment costs that aid the production or procurement of 
public, educational, and governmental programs. ETI Grant funds should be used to 
support education technology initiatives of boards of education and other education entities. 
B. 
ORDERS 
For orders requiring a filing, please submit an electronic version through the 
Authority’s website, at www.ct.gov/pura. Submissions filed in compliance with the 
Authority’s orders must be identified by: Docket Number, Title, and Order Number. 
1. 
No later than June 1, 2024, all grant recipients must complete, sign, and return a 
completed Agency Vendor Form (link in Appendix B) and Form W-9 (link in 
Appendix C), via e-mail to the DEEP Business Office, Teddi.Ezzo@ct.gov. The 
Agency Vendor Form and Form W-9 do not need to be filed with PURA 
electronically. 
2. 
No later than January 3, 2025, all grant recipients must file copies of all receipts 
and/or paid invoices for equipment and approved costs purchased with grant 
funds. All unused funds must be returned to the DEEP Business Office prior to 
receiving a new grant award. 
3. 
No later than January 3, 2025, PEG grant recipients must file a report stating (a) 
the title, subject, and duration (in minutes) of all community access programs 
facilitated in whole or in part by the grant award; (b) how the programs were 
distributed through community access channels; and (c) the protocols for ensuring 
that any programs produced with equipment purchased with PEGPETIA funds are 
made available to the applicant’s local PEG studio. 
4. 
No later than January 3, 2025, all grant recipients must file a report of the project 
enabled by the grant funds.
